name: SiteTallyWiz
author: FullStackWiz

sections.description:
SiteTallyWiz is a public visit counter, not an analytics dashboard. It shows one friendly number to your visitors, for example “1,234 visits”, and keeps nothing else about them. If you want a clean badge in your footer and no reports to wade through, this is it.

The number is sent by a small script after the page loads, so page caching plugins (LiteSpeed, WP Rocket, and similar) cannot freeze it.

What makes it different

  • One number, nothing else. By default the only thing stored for good is the total. No cookies, no stored IP addresses, no visitor profiles, no admin reports to maintain.
  • Cache-safe by design. The page can be fully cached; the count is fetched after load.
  • A modern, tidy pill. Dark pill, light pill, frosted-glass pill or minimal text, with your own accent colour, a gently pulsing dot and a short count-up animation. Animation is switched off for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
  • Starting number. Moving from another counter? Carry over your earlier total.
  • Your own label. “visits”, “views” or any short word of your choice.
  • Place it where you want. Automatic footer placement, an optional CSS selector to tuck it into your theme’s footer, the [sitetallywiz] shortcode ([sitetallywiz label="Readers"]), or the SiteTallyWiz Counter block in the block editor.
  • Two ways to count. Every page load (stores nothing about the visitor) or once per visitor every N minutes (1 to 1440).
  • Sensible exclusions. Skips bots, logged-in editors, user roles you choose, and a keyword list you can edit.
  • Settings export and import (JSON), to copy your setup between sites.
  • Accessible. role="status", readable label, reduced-motion respected.
  • Privacy-policy text included and all data removed when you delete the plugin.
  • Small on purpose. One admin page, two public REST routes, no external requests.

No ads, no upsell, no “powered by” link, no tracking. Free, and every feature is included.

Privacy

SiteTallyWiz sets no cookies and never stores IP addresses.

  • In the default mode only one number is stored: the total.
  • To limit abuse, a one-way salted hash made from the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent is kept for 60 seconds as a small rate limit. It cannot be turned back into an address and expires on its own.
  • If you choose “Once per visitor”, the same kind of hash is kept for the number of minutes you choose (at most 24 hours), then it expires.
  • Nothing is sent to other websites or services.
  • Suggested privacy policy text is added under Settings > Privacy.

Public endpoints and why they exist:

  • POST /wp-json/sitetallywiz/v1/hit is public because anonymous visitors have to be able to count themselves. It checks the request origin, ignores bots and rate-limits each client. It returns only the number.
  • GET /wp-json/sitetallywiz/v1/count is public and read-only. It returns only the number that is already shown on your site.

External services: none. The plugin makes no external requests, has no update checker and sends no telemetry.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the sitetallywiz folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate it. The counter appears in your footer straight away.
  3. Adjust it under Settings > SiteTallyWiz.
sections.faq:
How is this different from the analytics plugins?

SiteTallyWiz is not an analytics tool. It has no dashboard, no per-page reports and no visitor tracking. It simply shows a visit count to your visitors, in a style that matches your site.

Can I carry over the count from another counter?

Yes. Enter your previous total as the starting number under Settings > SiteTallyWiz.

Does it count every page load?

Yes, by default. A returning visitor raises the number again. If you prefer one count per visitor, choose “Once per visitor” in the settings.

Is the number exact?

No. It is a friendly indicator, not an audit. Anyone can call the public counting address, so a per-client limit and a bot filter keep it reasonable, but it is not meant for billing or reporting.

Will page caching freeze the number?

No. The page itself is cached, but the number is requested after the page loads.

The pill appears in the wrong place.

Enter a CSS selector such as footer .copyright under Settings > SiteTallyWiz, or switch placement to “Shortcode only” and put [sitetallywiz] where you want it.

Does it work with multisite?

It works on each site separately. Network-wide totals are not part of this version.
